correctness.rationale: For any specified k nonroot labels, deleting those k leaf-children of the root gives a bijection with all (n-k-1)! recursive trees on remaining vertices and preserves uniformity. This gives the exact mixed falling-factorial transform, with a separately handled all-star endpoint k=n-1. Eulerian leaf-count recursion and expansion of u^Q yield the full polynomial for every n≥2 and all complex u,z. Its derivatives yield E[QL]=(n+1)/2 and Cov(Q,L)=1/2 for n≥3. Marginal variances Var(Q)=1 and Var(L)=n/12 yield Corr=sqrt(3/n). The independent Poisson/Gaussian joint limit follows from a bounded 1-dependent descent CLT and dominated convergence of the mixed factorial transform, not finite experiments. The standalone verifier independently enumerated each (n-1)! tree for n=2,...,9 (46,233 total), checking all integer joint coefficients and all admissible factorial identities plus covariances in exact arithmetic. n=2 covariance exception is explicit.

originality.rationale: The new statement is a full finite-size bivariate law for the count of root children that are leaves together with all leaves, yielding covariance exactly 1/2 and a joint independent Poisson/Gaussian limit. Devroye–Janson (2013), Section 7, derives a Poisson-thinning marginal of root leaf-children in the time-indexed Yule tree, not the joint distribution conditioned on exactly n vertices. Mahmoud–Ward (2015), Sections 2–3, calculates means and variance growth for the total number of protected vertices, a different observable. Janson (2004/05) gives global outdegree-profile marginals. A previous root-degree/global-leaf covariance does not imply the present root leaf-child/global-leaf joint polynomial. No checked full primary text gives the bivariate statement or a directly dominating theorem; historical implicit derivability via classical increasing-tree generating functions remains a disclosed risk.

value.rationale: The number of root leaf-children controls whether the founding vertex is protected and how many immediate root branches are singletons, while the global number of leaves controls total terminal branching. These are different natural local/global observables in the same canonical random-growth tree. The result determines every finite bivariate coefficient, not merely a root-local mean, a known Eulerian marginal, or a trivial special case. It reveals a striking precise phenomenon: Cov(Q,L)=1/2 and positive Corr=sqrt(3/n) for every n>=3 while the unscaled root count and normalized global leaf fluctuations converge independently; the exact correction is useful for calibration of joint branching observables and finite-size random-tree models. The deletion bijection, complete law and asymptotic coupling are structurally motivated by protected-root versus whole-tree leaf behavior; no unsupported application theorem is asserted.
